name: Kansas

windshield.strip: along the top of the windshield, not below the AS1 line; nonreflective; not red, yellow or amber

frontSide.note: total light transmission with all sun screening devices combined; nonreflective

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined ('total light transmission'; 'light transmission' includes any safety glazing material)

medicalExemption.text: Limited: only clear, colorless UV-blocking film with at least 78% VLT (glazing+film meeting FMVSS 205 70%), with a signed statement from a licensed physician or optometrist identifying the occupant. No exemption for dark tint. A driver cited without the statement has 60 days to produce it or remove the film.

penalty.text: Driver: misdemeanor (class C unless repeat within one year, K.S.A. 8-2116); class C misdemeanor fine up to $500 (K.S.A. 21-6611). Installer: class C misdemeanor (8-1749c).

quotes: the total light transmission shall not be less than 35% when a sun screening device is used in conjunction with other existing sun screening devices.
A sun screening device when used in conjunction with the windshield shall be nonreflective and shall not be red, yellow or amber in color.
shall not extend downward beyond the AS1 line, which is clearly defined and marked
The material has a minimum visible light transmittance of 78%
Any person convicted of violating the provisions of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
for a class C misdemeanor, a sum not exceeding $500

helmet.conditions: Under 18 operator or passenger; eye protection for all operators unless 10-in. windscreen

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Instruction permit holders may not operate a wireless communication device while driving (K.S.A. 8-2,100; restricted licenses similar)

studdedTires.season: Nov 1 - Apr 15 (stud tires, K.A.R. 36-7-1); studded traction equipment Nov 1 - Apr 1 (K.A.R. 36-7-2)

radarDetector.note: No state ban on radar detectors in private passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

underglow.rule: Only white or amber light visible from directly in front; no red to the front; flashing lights prohibited except authorized; AG Opinion 2003-6 says 8-1729 may prohibit 'ground effect' or 'auto neon' lights in some instances

openQuestions: K.A.R. 36-7-1/36-7-2 stud dates read via search summaries of Cornell/Justia copies, not the Kansas Register directly.
Lift/frame height: no Kansas statute located.
Whether 8-1749a(h) misdemeanor is enforced as class C (8-2116) - inferred from statute text, no agency confirmation.
